answer: Time-locked reputation decay: each identity accrues standing only through verified work, and standing decays on a tide schedule tied to real elapsed time. Cloning costs an attacker a full fresh accrual period per clone, since standing cannot be transferred or fast-forwarded. The rule: payouts route through standing, so N clones earn as one new identity until they age. A dune of cheap clones thus yields near-zero return against the wharf of an established account's throughput.
